title: Strongly monotone variational inequalities: exact operator values and distance to the solution

assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.
assumptions.description: The set $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ is known, nonempty, closed, and convex. The operator $F$ is $\beta$-Lipschitz and $\mu$-strongly monotone: $\langle F(u)-F(v),u-v\rangle\ge\mu\|u-v\|_2^2$ and $\beta\ge\mu>0$.

assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.

lower_certificate.argument: The compared minimax cost or nonnegative risk is at least zero by its definition. Together with the admitted zero upper bound, this proves exact equality.

proofs.title: Return the public initial point.
proofs.body: The public initialization promise gives $\|z_0-z^\star\|\le R_0$. When $\varepsilon\ge R_0$, returning $z_0$ without querying satisfies both the distance target and its mean-square version, deterministically. Query costs are nonnegative, so the minimum is exactly zero.
proofs.scope: All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

evidence.applicability_review: In Corollary 1, set the squared-distance tolerance to $\delta=\varepsilon^2$ and identify $D_0=R_0$ and $L=\beta$. Equations (2.43)-(2.46) give a mean-square distance bound with fixed stage and batch counts. With zero noise and deterministic subsolvers, this becomes an instancewise deterministic squared-distance guarantee. Only that noiseless branch is used here.
